items.why: The report says "Each has a G band at 1580 cm-1 and a single, symmetric 2D band at about 2680-2700 cm-1" (Au 2681.1, Cu 2695.7) and concludes both are "graphene-like sp2 carbon".

It gives Au "D 1343.9 ... I_D/I_G (heights) 0.96" and Cu "D 1349 ± 5 ... I_D/I_G is about 0.56 with an uncertainty comparable to the value", which matches the rubric numbers and the poor constraint on Cu.

The report never gives the hypothesis that the stronger D on Au comes from strain during rapid solidification; it puts quenching down only to stress state and possible small domains, and it does not link strain to D.

It ties the D band to defects ("grain boundaries, vacancy or sp3 defects, or a very small domain size") and checks strain against the G and 2D shifts, but it never says strain alone cannot activate D or tests a strain explanation for D.

It asks "What laser wavelength was used on each system?" and says the answer "decides whether the 14.6 cm-1 2D offset is physical" and is "required for any L_D estimate"; it also notes 2D dispersion of about 100 cm-1/eV and the λ^4 term.

It states "the Cu signal is weak ... Cu intensity ratios and weak-band statements are unreliable" (SNR about 9 against 26), says "Cu D and G fit uncertainties are comparable to the values", and gives explicit error bars.

wrong_claims.why: Although it is hedged, the report gives "L_D of about 12 nm" for Au using "the assumed 532 nm" and lists it under the L_D_nm property, even though the wavelength is unknown.
The report never says strain causes the Au D peak; it puts D down to defects or small domains.
